note: Two of the three games ran the full 60 s at 38 pipes, which is about the cap. Seed202 died at 12 on the bottom lip of a pipe it had just cleared. The game checks pipes[0] for a collision before it removes a passed pipe, and it reads pipe positions from the previous 16 ms page frame, so a pipe still counts for one frame after the bird's box is past its right edge. v2 dropped the pipe a frame early and reported marginIfWait 29 at the fatal frame, and its approach relied on that exit that did not exist. The lookahead now keeps each pipe active until one frame after the bird clears it (two frames when the last tick ran no game frame). It uses the game's hitbox width, which narrows as the bird tilts, for entry and exit, and it averages the bird's x to remove rounding. The rule and the fields are unchanged.
instructions:
Play the game well. Flappy Bird. Press Space (or click) to flap: the bird jumps up, then gravity pulls it down. Fly through the gaps between the pipes without touching a pipe or the ground. One point for every pipe passed.
Decide every 16 ms (one game frame): flap or wait. If over is true: wait. If playing is false (splash screen): flap to start. Otherwise flap only when flapEffect is "moreRoom" (flapping now keeps more clearance than not flapping this frame, i.e. marginIfFlap > marginIfWait). When flapEffect is "same" or "lessRoom", wait.
marginIfFlap and marginIfWait are the best worst-case clearance in px the bird can keep over the next ~1 s if it flaps now or does not flap this frame. Every later flap is assumed to be timed as well as possible: frame by frame for the next 10 frames, then every 2-3 frames. Clearance is measured to the gap edges for as long as the game tests the pipe (from when the bird's tilted hitbox reaches the pipe's left edge until one frame after the hitbox is past its right edge), to the ground, and to a band that widens with distance around the upcoming gaps. It is capped at 190. A value below -200 (crashIfFlap / crashIfWait true) means a crash can't be avoided; less negative means the crash comes later.
The other fields are context. vel is px per 60 Hz frame (+ is down). roomToGround is the px left above the ground. pipeDx / msToPipe are the distance and time until the bird's front enters the next pipe (inPipe is true while inside it). msToClear is the time until the bird is past that pipe. roomAbove / roomBelow are the px between the bird's hitbox and that gap's top and bottom edges. nextGapShift is how much lower (+) or higher (-) the following gap is. passed is the number of pipes cleared. unknownThing is an unrecognised object ahead; treat it as an obstacle.

actions.description: Click once: the bird jumps (velocity set to -4.6 px/frame, rising about 40 px over the next 0.3 s before falling again). On the splash screen this starts the game.
Do nothing this frame. Gravity keeps pulling the bird down (+0.25 px/frame each frame).

tests.why: Frames around v1 t=98-100: the bird is high after the 92-182 gap and the 212-302 gap is 0.6-0.75 s away. It can survive by diving and then flapping at the right frame, but the 6-frame planner reported a certain crash with both actions. Frame-level planning must find a way through.

Frames around v1 t=129-131: dropping into the 156-246 gap is possible if the flap comes at the right frame (~frame 18). v1 flickered between crash and alive here. The new planner must see that the bird can survive.

Frames around v1 t=601-603, inside the 241-331 gap: holding off and flapping a few frames later keeps 5-10 px of clearance. v1's 6-frame grid called waiting a crash, and the game was lost two ticks later.

tests.expect: state.over || !state.playing || (state.flapEffect === 'moreRoom' ? state.marginIfFlap >= state.marginIfWait : state.flapEffect === 'lessRoom' ? state.marginIfFlap <= state.marginIfWait : state.flapEffect === 'same')
tests.why: The categorical flapEffect field that the rule reads must always exist and agree with the two margins.

tests.expect: !(state.playing && state.inPipe && state.vel >= 4.6 && state.vel <= 4.8 && state.roomBelow >= 3 && state.roomBelow <= 6 && state.pipeDx <= -80) || state.marginIfWait <= 2
tests.why: v2 t=1549-1550: the bird falls at 4.7 px/frame, 5 px above the bottom lip, and its front is about 83 px past the pipe. The pipe is geometrically cleared, but the game still tests it on the next frame because it removes a passed pipe only after the collision check. The game ended there, while v2 reported marginIfWait 29. Not flapping must show no real clearance.

tests.expect: state.over || !state.playing || (state.flapEffect === 'moreRoom' ? state.marginIfFlap >= state.marginIfWait : state.flapEffect === 'lessRoom' ? state.marginIfFlap <= state.marginIfWait : state.flapEffect === 'same')
tests.why: The rule reads only flapEffect, so it must always agree with the two margins, including during the tight pipe exit where the new pipe-removal model changes them.
